verdict.rationale: Dagster's documented schedules run jobs at intervals ranging from hourly, daily and weekly to arbitrary cron expressions. Declarative Automation adds per-asset on_cron conditions and sensors add event-driven triggers, so frequency is set per pipeline. On-demand runs appear in the docs only through running dbt subsets from the UI/APIs and triggering Airbyte syncs. missing for 10: explicit documentation of sub-hour (e.g. every-15-minute) scheduling, first-party docs for generic manual/ad-hoc run launching beyond integration examples, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a data engineer, I control sync frequency per pipeline — from sub-hour schedules to cron expressions and manual triggers

citations.quote: These intervals can range from common frequencies like hourly, daily, or weekly, to more complex patterns defined using cron expressions.
The AutomationCondition.on_cron will execute an asset once per cron schedule tick, after all upstream dependencies have updated.
Use Dagster's UI or APIs to run subsets of your dbt models, seeds, and snapshots.
you can trigger Airbyte syncs and orchestrate your Airbyte connections from within Dagster
